current_pipeline_status.reason: Supplied reports show unresolved label-definition, leakage, event-conditioning, overlapping-sample, calibration, and baseline-selection risks. The best reported squeeze configurations are negative or approximately flat after the stated 14 bps round-trip cost, and the strong-contrarian economic backtest path uses future-derived sweep label columns.

most_likely_bottleneck.reason: Across the audits, weak economic results are more plausibly explained by endpoint-return label mismatch, future-oracle execution risk, event-conditioned evaluation, overlapping windows, missing event-level purge, and insufficient baseline controls than by CatBoost hyperparameters.

catboost_should_be_kept.reason: CatBoost models are already present and can serve as controlled baselines. However, topology-only underperforms calendar-only for direction_1h in the supplied ablation, and supplied backtests do not show robust positive net expectancy after costs. Further CatBoost tuning should wait until labels, leakage controls, sampling, calibration, and baseline comparisons are fixed.

blocking_issues.reason: scripts/research_topology_v2_squeeze_events.py is referenced but not supplied, so squeeze_event_dataset and detected_squeeze_events construction, precursor semantics, event clustering, volatility quantile calculation, and leakage properties are unknown.

scripts/backtest_topology_v2_strong_contrarian_25bp.py loads sweep_code_1h and first_hit_seconds_1h, which are generated by inspecting future prices, and uses them in simulate_candidate to determine trade inclusion and timing.

direction_1h is an endpoint forward-return label, while a separate first-touch sweep label builder exists. The intended topology question appears path-dependent, and supplied reports do not quantify disagreement between endpoint direction and first-touch sweep outcomes.

squeeze_signal consumes walk_forward_predictions.parquet rather than every chronological 1h topology snapshot, and top configurations report event_rate = 1.0. The full-stream report separately states that it scores chronological 1h snapshots.
Both squeeze reports evaluate 7776 configurations and select top configurations from the same report. No untouched final chronological holdout after grid selection is supplied.

Every row receives forward labels over 15m, 1h, and 4h horizons, and the 1h model reports hundreds of thousands of sampled rows. No supplied core model report shows non-overlapping or block-bootstrap metrics.
The supplied 1h ablation shows calendar_only test balanced_accuracy of 0.450118, topology_only 0.403844, and combined 0.440963. Feature importance is dominated by symbol and calendar fields.

The best full-stream squeeze configuration reports event_precision 0.694444 and direction_accuracy 0.92 but mean_net_bps -3.333309 and profit_factor 0.792415. The best squeeze_signal configuration reports event_rate 1.0 and event_direction_accuracy 0.985294 but mean_net_bps -0.049520 and profit_factor 0.995597.

Backtests threshold CatBoost probabilities and direction_confidence, but supplied reports do not include ECE, Brier score, reliability curves, or confidence-bucket output files. Top configurations are unchanged across several minimum_direction_confidence values.
Duplicate id checks are present, but no supplied artifact reports duplicate symbol/timeframe/logged_at counts or stable event-key intersections across train, validation, and test.

experiments.title: Freeze and reproduce squeeze-event label generation

hypothesis.statement: The squeeze-event labels can be rebuilt deterministically from raw or feature inputs without future leakage beyond the declared target windows.

implementation: Provide scripts/research_topology_v2_squeeze_events.py and a small reproducible input sample.
Rebuild detected_squeeze_events.parquet, squeeze_event_dataset.parquet, and walk_forward_predictions.parquet inputs where applicable.
Create unit tests for precursor window boundaries, event window boundaries, volatility quantile thresholds, overlapping event clustering, and class assignment.
Record input hashes, output hashes, row counts, class counts, time ranges, and command parameters.
experiments.comparison: Rebuilt outputs versus existing artifacts by row count, event count, class distribution, id-level label equality, and hash where deterministic.
experiments.failure_interpretation: If labels cannot be reproduced exactly or label timing cannot be verified, squeeze-model and squeeze-backtest metrics remain unauditable and should not guide research decisions.
dependencies: raw or canonical feature input sample
existing squeeze output artifacts for comparison
leakage_checks: No feature used for precursor rows may be computed after logged_at.
Volatility quantiles must be computed only from historical data available before each fold decision point.
Target_event fields must not be present in feature matrices except as targets or evaluation fields.

experiments.title: Cross-tab endpoint direction, first-touch sweep, BOTH, INVALID, and strong-contrarian labels

hypothesis.statement: Endpoint direction_1h materially disagrees with first-touch sweep labels often enough that it should not be treated as the primary liquidation-topology target without qualification.

implementation: Join liq_topology_v2_ml_labeled.parquet, liq_topology_v2_sweep_labels.parquet, and strong_contrarian labels where available by id.
For 1h rows, cross-tab direction_1h against sweep_code_1h.
Report INVALID, NONE, LOWER_FIRST, UPPER_FIRST, and BOTH counts by symbol, timeframe, fold, and volatility decile if volatility features are available.
For BOTH rows, inspect first-hit timestamp resolution, inter-snapshot interval, and price move size where source data permits.
Define explicit downstream policy for BOTH and INVALID before model training.
experiments.comparison: Endpoint direction labels versus first-touch sweep labels, and first-touch labels versus strong-contrarian labels where available.
experiments.failure_interpretation: If sign conflict exceeds the pre-set threshold or BOTH/INVALID rates are unstable, endpoint direction and first-touch sweep must be modeled and reported as separate tasks.
leakage_checks: Use label columns only for audit outputs, not as model features.
Confirm joins do not duplicate ids.
Report unmatched id counts.

experiments.title: Measure duplicate timestamps, overlapping windows, event clustering, and non-overlapping metric degradation

hypothesis.statement: Dense overlapping snapshots and repeated timestamps materially reduce effective independent sample size relative to reported row counts.

implementation: Group feature rows by symbol, timeframe, and logged_at to count duplicate timestamp rows.
Compute duplicate share, duplicate price share, and whether duplicate groups cross train, validation, or test boundaries.
Compute label autocorrelation and prediction autocorrelation at multiple snapshot lags for each symbol/timeframe.
Construct non-overlapping horizon buckets and keep one row per symbol/timeframe/bucket.
Recompute available model metrics on dense rows versus non-overlapping rows.
Estimate confidence intervals using day-level or symbol-day block bootstrap.
experiments.comparison: Dense row-level metrics versus non-overlapping bucket metrics and block-bootstrap intervals.
experiments.failure_interpretation: If metrics degrade materially or confidence intervals overlap baselines, row-level model results should be treated as overconfident and not used for final selection.
leakage_checks: Non-overlapping buckets must be formed independently within each split.
No rows with overlapping target windows may be used across train and evaluation periods when estimating final metrics.

experiments.title: Replace label-column execution with causal chronological trigger simulation

hypothesis.statement: A causal simulator using only signal-time levels and future observed prices can reproduce the label-driven strong-contrarian trade set; if not, the label-driven backtest is not executable evidence.

implementation: Remove sweep_code_1h, first_hit_seconds_1h, post_hit_continuation_pct_1h, and strong_contrarian labels from signal selection and entry timing.
At logged_at, place a virtual far-side trigger using levels known at logged_at.
Advance through the chronological price stream sequentially.
Enter only when the observed price crosses the trigger.
Apply cancellation, stop, target, post-entry window, cooldown, and cost assumptions without using future label columns.
Compare causal trade ids, entry timestamps, trigger rates, and returns against the existing label-driven simulator.
experiments.comparison: Label-driven simulator versus oracle-free chronological simulator.

minimum_success_threshold.for_economic_reporting: all headline metrics must come from the oracle-free simulator

experiments.failure_interpretation: If the causal simulator does not reproduce the label-driven trade set and timing, retire the label-driven economic report and treat it only as an outcome-label diagnostic.
dependencies: model probabilities if used for signal selection
leakage_checks: Static check for zero references to future-derived label columns in signal and execution code.
Execution code may read future prices only through sequential simulation after order placement.
All order parameters must be determined at or before logged_at.

experiments.title: Evaluate squeeze and event models with full-stream scoring, event-level purge, and untouched outer holdout

hypothesis.statement: Reported squeeze performance changes when evaluation is full-stream, event-level purged, and separated into inner selection and outer final evaluation.

implementation: Attach stable event keys where event labels exist, such as symbol plus event time plus event direction or other deterministic event identifier.
Score every chronological 1h topology snapshot in each test fold, not only event-oriented prediction rows.
Use inner folds for threshold and execution-grid selection.
Evaluate exactly one frozen selected configuration on an untouched later chronological outer holdout.
Purge training rows whose label windows overlap validation or test intervals.
Purge rows sharing the same stable event key across train, validation, and test.
experiments.comparison: Existing squeeze_signal and full_stream reports versus purged full-stream nested walk-forward results.
experiments.failure_interpretation: If performance deteriorates under full-stream nested purged evaluation, prior signal or full-stream reports should be treated as model-selection diagnostics rather than final evidence.
leakage_checks: No event key may appear in more than one split within a fold.
No training label window may overlap validation or test time ranges.
Thresholds and execution settings must be selected only inside inner folds.

experiments.title: Establish mandatory no-trade, calendar, symbol, distance-only, and simple-rule baselines

hypothesis.statement: Some observed model performance can be matched by simpler baselines such as calendar/symbol or distance-only rules.

implementation: For each target family, train or compute baselines on identical purged walk-forward folds.
Include no-trade baseline in every economic summary.
Include majority or base-rate baseline for classification.

Include calendar_only, symbol_only, calendar_plus_symbol, topology_only, topology_without_symbol, distance_only, nearest_side, and deterministic distance_advantage threshold baselines where applicable.
For economic tests, apply the same oracle-free execution assumptions to model and baseline signals.
experiments.comparison: Full model versus no-trade, base-rate, calendar/symbol, distance-only, nearest-side, and deterministic liquidity-distance baselines.
experiments.failure_interpretation: If simple baselines match the full model within equivalence margins, prioritize the simpler baseline or revisit the target before adding features or tuning.
dependencies: oracle-free execution simulator for economic comparisons
leakage_checks: All baselines and full models use identical split boundaries.
Calendar and symbol features must be available at logged_at.
Distance-only features must be computed from signal-time topology levels only.

experiments.title: Audit probability calibration, confidence thresholds, and abstention behavior

hypothesis.statement: Raw model probabilities and direction_confidence are not sufficiently calibrated or monotonic to support fixed confidence thresholds without validation-fold calibration.

implementation: Compute reliability curves, ECE, MCE, Brier score, log_loss, and bucketed event rates for each fold.
Report bucketed metrics by symbol, timeframe, and confidence decile.
Compare raw probabilities with validation-only temperature scaling, isotonic calibration, and Platt calibration where applicable.
Plot or tabulate coverage, event rate, direction accuracy, and mean net bps by probability and confidence threshold.
Require thresholds to be selected only on validation or inner folds.
experiments.comparison: Raw probabilities versus validation-calibrated probabilities, and low-confidence versus high-confidence cohorts.
experiments.failure_interpretation: If probabilities are not calibrated or thresholds do not change coverage or quality, treat confidence thresholds as inactive diagnostics and do not use them for selection.
dependencies: trade outputs if economic buckets are evaluated
leakage_checks: Calibration models must be fit only on validation or inner-fold data.
Test and outer-holdout labels may not be used to choose calibration method or thresholds.

experiments.title: Measure whether event labels imply tradable post-cost paths

hypothesis.statement: High event precision and direction accuracy fail economically because events are too late, too small, too volatile, or poorly aligned with stop and target geometry after costs.

implementation: For every alert, compute post-alert and post-entry MFE, MAE, time to favorable excursion, time to adverse excursion, stop hit, target hit, and net bps after stated costs.
Stratify by true event class, predicted class, direction correctness, lead time, probability bucket, symbol, timeframe, and fold.
Compare event-positive/economic-positive rows against event-positive/economic-negative rows.
Test fixed target/stop, nearest-liquidity target/stop, and volatility-scaled exits only under oracle-free simulation.
experiments.comparison: Event-detected versus no-event alerts, direction-correct versus direction-incorrect alerts, and alternative pre-registered exit geometries.

minimum_success_threshold.diagnostic_requirement: all selected event labels must show economic separation between event_positive_economic_positive and event_positive_economic_negative cohorts
minimum_success_threshold.strategy_promotion_gate: positive post-cost outer-holdout metrics required before any strategy claim

experiments.failure_interpretation: If event-positive alerts do not have better post-cost MFE/MAE or target-before-stop profiles, event labels should remain diagnostic and not be used as direct trade objectives.
leakage_checks: Exit geometry must be pre-specified from signal-time information.
MFE and MAE may be used for evaluation and label design, not for live signal selection unless converted into a separately trained time-safe target.

experiments.title: Test stability by symbol, timeframe, volatility, trend, and matrix/topology regime

hypothesis.statement: Aggregate performance hides unstable behavior across symbols, timeframes, folds, and regimes.

implementation: Report metrics by fold, symbol, timeframe, symbol_timeframe, and volatility decile.
If matrix/regime features are available with verified timestamp alignment, add regime cohorts such as trend alignment, topology/matrix agreement, and conflict.
Run leave-one-symbol-out and leave-one-timeframe-out validation for primary targets.
Compute worst-group metrics and dispersion, not only aggregate averages.
Mark unsupported groups if sample counts or validation metrics fail pre-registered gates.
experiments.comparison: Aggregate model performance versus worst-group, macro-group, leave-one-symbol-out, and leave-one-timeframe-out performance.
experiments.failure_interpretation: If performance is concentrated in a few groups or fails held-out groups, restrict scope or redesign features/targets before model tuning.

leakage_checks: Regime tags must be computed using only data available at logged_at or after candle close as appropriate.
Leave-one-group-out splits must not include the held-out group in training.

experiments.title: Add backward-only dynamic topology and volatility-normalized feature blocks

hypothesis.statement: Temporal topology behavior and volatility-normalized distances add more transferable signal than static raw distances and log volumes alone.

implementation: Create backward-only features such as level_age_minutes, nearest_side_stability_minutes, distance_velocity, pool_volume_velocity, active_level_velocity, prior_sweep_count, post_sweep_elapsed_minutes, and cluster_persistence_score if source data supports them.

Create volatility-normalized features such as distance_to_recent_realized_volatility, distance_to_ATR, liquidity_pressure_per_volatility, and volume relative to rolling symbol/timeframe baselines if source data supports them.
Use a feature-family registry to prevent uncontrolled raw/log/ratio duplication.
Evaluate blocks under identical purged walk-forward folds after baseline experiments are complete.
experiments.comparison: Static topology versus dynamic topology, volatility-normalized topology, dynamic plus normalized topology, and full feature set.
experiments.failure_interpretation: If dynamic or normalized blocks do not improve locked baselines under purged folds, do not expand feature complexity; revisit targets or data quality instead.
leakage_checks: All rolling features must be backward-only within symbol/timeframe.
Rolling normalizers must not be fit on validation or test future rows.
Matrix or candle-derived features must be available only after candle close.

experiments.title: Compare multiclass softmax against explicit event model plus conditional direction model

implementation: Train Stage 1 as event/no-event or economic-edge/no-edge model.
Train Stage 2 as conditional direction model on event-positive or valid first-touch rows only.
Generate out-of-fold probabilities for both stages.
Compare against existing multiclass squeeze probability and direction_confidence construction.
Apply abstention based on both event probability and conditional direction confidence selected only on validation folds.
experiments.comparison: Single multiclass model versus two-stage event plus conditional direction model at matched alert coverage.
experiments.failure_interpretation: If two-stage modeling does not improve calibration or event-conditioned direction at matched coverage, retain the simpler multiclass baseline and focus on labels/features rather than architecture.
dependencies: oracle-free simulator if economic metrics are included
leakage_checks: Stage 2 training rows must be selected using true labels only within training folds.
Validation and test event labels may not determine live-stage routing except for evaluation.
